review_output: {"summary":"I reviewed only the changed retry logic and the deadlock recovery evidence. The classifier is narrow: a plain Error, a P2002 unique violation and lock-timeout codes are not retried. Payment webhooks keep 2 attempts and inventory keeps 3. The crossed-lock harness shows that a real deadlock surfacing as PrismaClientUnknownRequestError is accepted and that a fresh test transaction then succeeds. Not ready: it's still unproven that a deadlock inside the real webhook callback is recovered, because the wrapper tests make getDb throw. The open lock-order MAJOR from the prior 116 review and the 7/20 synchronized20 SSI failure are out of scope here and still block the WP.","findings":[{"area":"Payment webhook deadlock recovery","severity":"MAJOR","file":"src/lib/payment-webhooks.ts","issue":"Retrying after a deadlock inside processPaymentWebhookOnce is unproven. Inside the real callback the error may look different: wrapped in a domain error, caught and the event marked failed, or replaced by a P2028 or 25P02 error from a parallel query on the aborted transaction. The classifier rejects all of these. A retry also re-runs any work done outside the transaction.","evidence":"The wrapper tests make getDb throw, so no transaction ever starts. The observed error came from the harness's sequential tx.paymentTransaction.update, not from the webhook's transaction.","impact":"In production, deadlocks may still return 5xx or leave the event in a failed state without retrying. A retry could also duplicate side effects.","recommended_fix":"Force a crossed lock inside the real webhook transaction. Make sure the deadlock error reaches the retry wrapper unwrapped, and that any work outside the transaction is idempotent.","required_test":"Integration test: a side connection holds the order/payment row locks in reverse order while processPaymentWebhook runs. Assert there is exactly one rejected attempt, the second attempt commits, and there is exactly one commission/ledger row and one processed event.","confidence":0.7},{"area":"Retry budget","severity":"MINOR","file":"src/lib/payment-webhooks.ts","issue":"Deadlocks now use the existing 2-attempt webhook budget, but the retry runs immediately with no delay. The lock-order MAJOR is still open, so the same crossed schedule is likely to collide again.","evidence":"for attempt<2 loop with no delay; runSerializable in inventory-reservations.ts also retries with no backoff","impact":"The one webhook retry can be used up by a predictable second collision, leaving delivery to the provider's redelivery.","recommended_fix":"Add a small random delay before retrying and keep the attempt counts at 2 and 3.","required_test":"Unit test with fake timers: the retry waits for a delay inside the expected bounds, and the call count stays 2 for webhooks and 3 for inventory.","confidence":0.6},{"area":"Classifier tests","severity":"MINOR","file":"src/lib/database-write-conflict.test.ts","issue":"No test covers the 'kind: Deadlock' pattern. The negative cases have no UnknownRequestError carrying lock-timeout or other connector-error text. The inventory 3-attempt budget is not tested with an UnknownRequestError deadlock.","evidence":"Only the 'ERROR: deadlock detected' text is tested as a positive case; the only negative UnknownRequestError is 'synthetic unrelated failure'.","impact":"A regression in either regex branch, or in the inventory budget, would go unnoticed.","recommended_fix":"Add a 'kind: Deadlock' positive case. Add negative UnknownRequestError cases with lock timeout/55P03 and 'could not obtain lock' text. Add a test that runSerializable makes exactly 3 attempts on a deadlock.","required_test":"New unit cases for each pattern, plus an inventory test that counts $transaction calls.","confidence":0.75},{"area":"Deadlock harness evidence","severity":"MINOR","file":"scripts/wp20-order-payment-deadlock.mjs","issue":"Each loop iteration overwrites the diagnostic file, so only the last of the 9 pairs is kept. The harness never asserts the error is an UnknownRequestError with deadlock text. In all 9 runs the payment transaction lost, so the order-loser branch never ran. The classifier is passed in as a parameter, so whether it is the real exported function depends on a runner that wasn't supplied.","evidence":"writeFileSync is inside the loop; every result has aborted:'payment'; isDatabaseWriteConflict is a function argument.","impact":"The evidence for the 'observed driver deadlock' claim covers less than it appears to.","recommended_fix":"Collect diagnostics for every pair and write them once. Assert error.name and the deadlock-message flag. Import the classifier from src in the harness or the runner.","required_test":"Rerun and save 9 diagnostics, each with type=PrismaClientUnknownRequestError and deadlockMessage=true.","confidence":0.7},{"area":"Naming","severity":"NIT","file":"src/lib/inventory-reservations.ts","issue":"The name isSerializableConflict is now misleading, since it also matches deadlocks.","evidence":"isSerializableConflict now simply returns isDatabaseWriteConflict(error).","impact":"Readability only.","recommended_fix":"Call isDatabaseWriteConflict directly.","required_test":"None.","confidence":0.6}]}
